title: China Price Check: $96 Blue Lagoon or $7 Hot Springs? | China Travel Expert
description:
Iceland's Blue Lagoon costs about $96 to soak. China's volcanic hot springs? About $7 just to walk in — which one are you booking?

Iceland's Blue Lagoon starts around $96 for its basic Comfort entry, and dynamic pricing pushes it higher on busy dates. In Yunnan's volcano country, Tengchong's Rehai ("Sea of Heat") geothermal park charges about ¥50 (~$7) to enter, where you can see the boiling pools and soak in designated hot-spring areas; a ¥120 combined ticket adds the volcano park next door. Even a full private hot-spring bath at a Tengchong resort runs roughly ¥228 (~$32) — still about a third of the Blue Lagoon price. Same volcanic heat, a fraction of the cost.

🧭 Expert Tip: Tengchong's Rehai is quietest on weekday mornings; grab the combined ¥120 ticket to add the volcano park, and bring a swimsuit for the bathing pools.
